plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A cormous perennial that produces goblet-shaped flowers in autumn, long after its leaves have died back. The blooms emerge directly from the soil without foliage, which is why it is sometimes called 'naked ladies'. All parts of the plant are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (September-October in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of Europe and North Africa; widely cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and used by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust native wildflower with dense clusters of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It thrives in moist meadows and roadsides and is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Quebec to Alabama and west to the Rockies
plants.funFact: New England Asters are a key fuel stop for migrating monarch butterflies heading to Mexico in early October.

plants.name: Osmanthus fragrans
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree bearing clusters of tiny, intensely fragrant flowers with a scent reminiscent of apricots and peaches. It is widely planted in gardens, temples, and parks across East Asia.
plants.location: Native to China, Japan, and the Himalayas; cultivated in Asia and the southern United States
plants.funFact: In China, osmanthus blossoms are celebrated during the Mid-Autumn Festival and used to flavor tea, cakes, wine, and jam.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular deciduous to semi-evergreen tree that covers itself with clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers before the new leaves emerge. It is a signature street tree in subtropical cities of the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, the jacaranda bloom is so iconic that the city is nicknamed 'Jacaranda City', and an old student superstition says a falling blossom on your head brings good luck in exams.
